::: {#sol-choose-distribution}

The outcome is a count: a non-negative whole number with no fixed upper limit.
The [Poisson distribution](#def-poisson) is a natural first choice for such an outcome,
because its values are $0, 1, 2, \ldots$.
A [Bernoulli](#def-bernoulli) outcome has only two values,
and a [Gaussian](#def-normal) outcome can be negative or fractional,
so neither matches the weekly count.

If the weekly counts vary more than a Poisson distribution allows,
the [negative binomial distribution](#def-nb) is the next candidate.

:::
